segments.text: This video on ionizing radiation safety is to help you and your supervisor address radiation
segments.zh: 这部关于电离辐射安全的视频，旨在帮助你和你的主管处理你们科室的辐射

segments.text: safety in your section.
segments.zh: 安全问题。

segments.text: It should be reviewed annually to satisfy initial and refresher radiation safety training.
segments.zh: 应每年观看一次，以满足初始辐射安全培训和复训的要求。

segments.text: After viewing this tape, please take a few minutes to discuss radiation safety procedures
segments.zh: 看完这部录像后，请花几分钟讨论一下与你们区域

segments.text: that pertain to your area.
segments.zh: 相关的辐射安全程序。

segments.text: With informed workers, responsible supervisors, and an aggressive safety program, we can reach
segments.zh: 有了知情的工作人员、负责的主管和积极有力的安全计划，我们就能实现

segments.text: our goal of keeping all exposures to ionizing radiation a lara or as low as reasonably achievable.
segments.zh: 我们的目标，使所有电离辐射照射都保持 ALARA，即合理可行尽量低。

segments.text: Ionizing radiation is used throughout the Air Force in a multitude of applications.
segments.zh: 整个空军在许许多多的应用中都会使用电离辐射。

segments.text: Whether it's used to see inside a body or an aircraft part, ionizing radiation is high
segments.zh: 无论是用来观察人体内部还是飞机零件内部，电离辐射都具有很高的

segments.text: energy and must be strictly controlled to prevent or reduce exposures.
segments.zh: 能量，必须严格控制，以防止或减少照射。

segments.text: This type of radiation emission includes high energy photons like x-rays and gamma rays
segments.zh: 这类辐射发射包括 X 射线和 γ 射线等高能光子，

segments.text: as well as particles like alpha, beta, and neutron radiation.
segments.zh: 以及 α、β 和中子辐射等粒子。

segments.text: Ionizing radiation is just another property of matter in the form of energy release that
segments.zh: 电离辐射只不过是物质的另一种属性，表现为一种

segments.text: occurs naturally.
segments.zh: 自然发生的能量释放。

segments.text: Whether it's coming from uranium or underground, rays from the sun or the cosmos, we are continually
segments.zh: 无论是来自铀或地下、来自太阳或宇宙的射线，我们一生中

segments.text: throughout our lives being exposed to naturally occurring background radiation.
segments.zh: 都在持续不断地受到天然本底辐射的照射。

segments.text: We can't control or limit background exposures, however, there is a lot we can do to control
segments.zh: 我们无法控制或限制本底照射，但是，我们可以做很多事情来控制

segments.text: and limit our occupational exposures.
segments.zh: 和限制我们的职业照射。

segments.text: Ionizing radiation can be generated by emitters that use large voltages to force electrons
segments.zh: 电离辐射可以由发射装置产生，这些装置利用高电压迫使电子

segments.text: to strike a target and release x-rays.
segments.zh: 撞击靶并释放出 X 射线。

segments.text: The x-rays generated are then filtered and collimated to produce x-rays of desirable strength.
segments.zh: 产生的 X 射线随后经过过滤和准直，得到所需强度的 X 射线。

segments.text: Ionizing radiation is also produced by the natural decay of radioactive materials.
segments.zh: 电离辐射也可以由放射性物质的自然衰变产生。

segments.text: When radioactive materials decay, they revert to a more stable form and release energy in
segments.zh: 放射性物质衰变时，会转变为更稳定的形态，并以下列一种或多种

segments.text: the form of one or more of the following.
segments.zh: 形式释放能量。

segments.text: Gamma rays, alpha particles, beta particles, neutrons, light, and heat.
segments.zh: γ 射线、α 粒子、β 粒子、中子、光和热。

segments.text: Different radioactive materials have different energy release signatures.
segments.zh: 不同的放射性物质有不同的能量释放特征。

segments.text: Radioactive materials are chosen on what type of energy release is required for the process.
segments.zh: 放射性物质是根据工艺需要哪种类型的能量释放来选择的。

segments.text: For example, a radioactive material called amorecium-241 is commonly used in smoke detectors
segments.zh: 例如，一种叫做镅-241 的放射性物质，常用于烟雾探测器

segments.text: and in lantern pods.
segments.zh: 和提灯部件中。

segments.text: Amorecium-241 emits an alpha and gamma radiation when it decays, which meets the required
segments.zh: 镅-241 衰变时会发出 α 和 γ 辐射，这满足了该系统所需的

segments.text: energy signature for the system.
segments.zh: 能量特征。

segments.text: It is important to note that materials that are irradiated do not normally become radioactive
segments.zh: 需要注意的是，受到照射的物质通常不会变成放射性的，

segments.text: unless they are subjected to extremely high radiation, as found in nuclear reactions.
segments.zh: 除非它们受到极高的辐射，比如核反应中的辐射。

segments.text: Most materials that are exposed to ionizing radiation remain essentially unaffected.
segments.zh: 大多数受到电离辐射照射的物质基本上不受影响。

segments.text: However, ionizing radiation can and often does damage to cells that are exposed to high
segments.zh: 但是，电离辐射能够、而且常常确实会损伤受到足够高水平照射的

segments.text: enough levels.
segments.zh: 细胞。

segments.text: This type of acute exposure is not likely to be significant unless large doses are
segments.zh: 这种急性照射不太可能有显著影响，除非接受了大剂量、

segments.text: received, repeated exposures are experienced.
segments.zh: 经历了反复照射、

segments.text: Large portions of the body are exposed and sensitive tissues are exposed.
segments.zh: 身体大部分受到照射，以及敏感组织受到照射。

segments.text: Ionizing can change the DNA structure producing a mutation.
segments.zh: 电离会改变 DNA 结构，产生突变。

segments.text: If the DNA is damaged at a certain spot and it can't repair itself, it may cause a tumor
segments.zh: 如果 DNA 在某个位置受损并且无法自我修复，就可能导致肿瘤

segments.text: or cancer.
segments.zh: 或癌症。

segments.text: When a DNA strand is mutated, the cell dies most of the time.
segments.zh: 当 DNA 链发生突变时，细胞大多数情况下会死亡。

segments.text: Repeated exposures increase the odds that one mutated cell will survive, producing a
segments.zh: 反复照射会增加某个突变细胞存活下来、形成

segments.text: cancerous growth.
segments.zh: 癌性生长的几率。

segments.text: Since more exposure equals more risk, all exposures must be minimized.
segments.zh: 由于照射越多风险越大，所有照射都必须尽量减少。

segments.text: We can minimize our exposures through four main control measures, time, distance, shielding
segments.zh: 我们可以通过四项主要控制措施来尽量减少照射：时间、距离、屏蔽

segments.text: and contamination control.
segments.zh: 和污染控制。

segments.text: Time.
segments.zh: 时间。

segments.text: When working with radiation sources, the more time personnel are exposed to the source,
segments.zh: 在使用辐射源时，人员暴露于辐射源的时间越长，

segments.text: the more radiation exposure personnel will receive.
segments.zh: 人员受到的辐射照射就越多。

segments.text: The exposure effects may be unnoticeable or negligible, but the overall dose is always
segments.zh: 照射的效应可能不易察觉或可以忽略，但总剂量始终

segments.text: considered cumulative.
segments.zh: 被视为是累积的。

segments.text: Therefore, careful steps must be taken to minimize exposure.
segments.zh: 因此，必须采取周密的步骤尽量减少照射。

segments.text: Steps like rehearsing a radiation procedure, adjusting a source's power output to what
segments.zh: 诸如预演辐射操作程序、把辐射源的功率输出调到

segments.text: is needed, and careful management of on times will prevent unnecessary retakes and reduce
segments.zh: 所需的水平、仔细管理开机时间等步骤，可以避免不必要的重拍，并减少

segments.text: the time the source is used.
segments.zh: 辐射源的使用时间。

segments.text: Distance.
segments.zh: 距离。

segments.text: The most effective method of minimizing radiation exposures is to simply increase the
segments.zh: 尽量减少辐射照射最有效的方法，就是增加

segments.text: distance between the source and the personnel exposed.
segments.zh: 辐射源与受照人员之间的距离。

segments.text: The inverse square law applies to radiation emissions, in that the radiation intensities
segments.zh: 平方反比定律适用于辐射发射，即辐射强度

segments.text: fall off very rapidly as the distance increases.
segments.zh: 随着距离的增加而迅速下降。

segments.text: For example, if the distance is doubled, the radiation intensity is reduced by a factor
segments.zh: 例如，如果距离加倍，辐射强度就会降为

segments.text: of four.
segments.zh: 四分之一。

segments.text: Obviously, a few feet may make a difference.
segments.zh: 显然，几英尺的距离就可能产生影响。

segments.text: Steps like keeping personnel as far away from the source as possible, establishing and maintaining
segments.zh: 诸如让人员尽可能远离辐射源、设立并维持

segments.text: controlled areas, and directing beams away from potentially occupied areas are extremely
segments.zh: 控制区，以及让射束避开可能有人的区域等步骤，都极其

segments.text: important.
segments.zh: 重要。

segments.text: Shielding.
segments.zh: 屏蔽。

segments.text: Any material placed between the source of the radiation and the potentially occupied
segments.zh: 放在辐射源和可能有人的区域之间的任何物质，

segments.text: areas will absorb some of the radiation and thus reduce exposures.
segments.zh: 都会吸收部分辐射，从而减少照射。

segments.text: In general, the more material used or the denser the material, the more radiation will
segments.zh: 一般来说，使用的物质越多或者物质密度越大，吸收的辐射就

segments.text: be absorbed.
segments.zh: 越多。

segments.text: Shielding is generally required when areas adjacent to the radiation source are potentially occupied.
segments.zh: 当辐射源附近的区域可能有人时，通常需要屏蔽。

segments.text: Good shielding begins with the proper design and installation of the shielding.
segments.zh: 良好的屏蔽始于屏蔽的正确设计和安装。

segments.text: Careful consideration must be followed for renovations to ensure the shielding is not
segments.zh: 进行改造时必须仔细考虑，确保屏蔽不会

segments.text: compromised.
segments.zh: 受到破坏。

segments.text: Shielding such as collimators must be used to restrict the beam to just the area of interest.
segments.zh: 必须使用准直器之类的屏蔽，把射束限制在感兴趣的区域内。

segments.text: Shielded facilities should be used whenever available or strict control measures must be
segments.zh: 只要有屏蔽设施就应使用，否则必须遵守

segments.text: followed.
segments.zh: 严格的控制措施。

segments.text: Last, simple shielding such as lead aprons must be used when required by the operation.
segments.zh: 最后，当操作需要时，必须使用铅围裙之类的简易屏蔽。

segments.text: Contamination control.
segments.zh: 污染控制。

segments.text: This mainly applies to the use of radioactive materials.
segments.zh: 这主要适用于放射性物质的使用。

segments.text: When a radioactive source is suspected of being broken or potentially leaking, it should
segments.zh: 当怀疑放射源破损或可能泄漏时，应当

segments.text: be isolated and the radiation safety officer, or RSO, consulted immediately.
segments.zh: 将其隔离，并立即咨询辐射安全官，即 RSO。

segments.text: Proper hygiene is the easiest and most effective measure to prevent radioactive materials from
segments.zh: 良好的卫生习惯是防止放射性物质沾到皮肤和衣服上、

segments.text: getting on the skin and close and to guard against accidental ingestion.
segments.zh: 并防止意外食入的最简单、最有效的措施。

segments.text: For all ionizing radiation operations, a radiation exposure assessment must be conducted
segments.zh: 对于所有电离辐射操作，都必须在首次进行该操作时

segments.text: during initial performance of the operation and revalidated annually.
segments.zh: 开展辐射照射评估，并每年重新确认。

segments.text: This survey is usually conducted by the base RSO, Bioenvironmental Engineer or Bioenvironmental
segments.zh: 这项调查通常由基地 RSO、生物环境工程师或生物环境

segments.text: Engineering Technician, and involves a detailed review of the operation and a review of the
segments.zh: 工程技术员进行，内容包括详细审查操作以及审查

segments.text: established or proposed safety measures.
segments.zh: 已建立或拟议的安全措施。

segments.text: Surveys are conducted using instruments such as an ionization chamber.
segments.zh: 调查使用电离室等仪器进行。

segments.text: Ion chambers are enclosed volumes of air or some other gas with electrodes placed inside
segments.zh: 电离室是一个充有空气或其他气体的封闭空间，内部装有电极，

segments.text: to collect ions produced by radiation.
segments.zh: 用来收集辐射产生的离子。

segments.text: By measuring the current, you can measure the relative radiation rate.
segments.zh: 通过测量电流，就可以测出相对辐射率。

segments.text: Geiger-Mueller or GM tubes like those commonly found in the ADM 300A Radiac set can also
segments.zh: 盖革-米勒管，即 GM 管，比如 ADM 300A 辐射检测仪（Radiac）中常见的那种，也可以

segments.text: be used for radiation detection.
segments.zh: 用于辐射探测。

segments.text: Radiation measurements are actually energy rates and are usually displayed in micro or
segments.zh: 辐射测量值实际上是能量率，通常以微伦琴或

segments.text: milli-renkins per hour.
segments.zh: 毫伦琴每小时为单位显示。

segments.text: Measurements are taken where all potential exposures may occur, including any possible public areas.
segments.zh: 测量要在所有可能发生照射的地方进行，包括任何可能的公共区域。

segments.text: The RSO or qualified technician then uses the measured radiation rates and reported usage
segments.zh: 然后，RSO 或合格的技术员利用测得的辐射率和报告的使用

segments.text: rates to determine the maximum worst-case exposure a worker or a member of the public
segments.zh: 率，来确定工作人员或公众

segments.text: could be exposed to.
segments.zh: 可能受到的最大最坏情况照射。

segments.text: In strict accordance with Title X, Code of Federal Regulations Part 20, Standards of
segments.zh: 严格按照美国联邦法规第 10 篇第 20 部分（10 CFR Part 20）《辐射防护标准》，

segments.text: Protection Against Radiation, workers may not be exposed to more than 5 REMs or Renkin's
segments.zh: 工作人员在一个日历年内受到的照射不得超过 5 雷姆，即伦琴

segments.text: equivalent MAN in a calendar year.
segments.zh: 当量人。

segments.text: Pregnant workers more than 0.5 REM during their pregnancy, and the public may not be
segments.zh: 孕期工作人员在整个孕期内不得超过 0.5 雷姆，公众每年受到的照射

segments.text: exposed to more than 0.1 REM per year.
segments.zh: 不得超过 0.1 雷姆。

segments.text: If the RSO determines that excessive exposure exists, engineering controls, personal protective
segments.zh: 如果 RSO 判定存在过量照射，可能会建议采取工程控制、个人防护

segments.text: equipment, and administrative controls to reduce the exposure potential may be recommended.
segments.zh: 装备和行政管理控制来降低照射的可能性。

segments.text: Based on the exposure potential, the RSO may decide to place personnel on a monthly or
segments.zh: 根据照射的可能性，RSO 可能会决定将人员纳入按月或

segments.text: quarterly dissimetry program.
segments.zh: 按季度的剂量监测计划。

segments.text: Certain jobs require personnel to be automatically placed in a dissimetry program.
segments.zh: 某些岗位要求人员自动纳入剂量监测计划。

segments.text: Pregnant radiation workers are required to be entered into monthly dissimetry.
segments.zh: 怀孕的辐射工作人员必须纳入按月剂量监测。

segments.text: For these personnel, the Base Bio-Environmental Engineering Office will assign Thermo-Luminescent
segments.zh: 对于这些人员，基地生物环境工程办公室会给每个人分配热释光

segments.text: Dissimeters, or TLDs, to each individual and collect them on a monthly or quarterly basis.
segments.zh: 剂量计，即 TLD，并按月或按季度收回。

segments.text: TLDs operate very simply by absorbing the radiation they are exposed to, and later release
segments.zh: TLD 的工作原理非常简单：它吸收所受到的辐射，之后

segments.text: that information when heated in a TLD reading instrument.
segments.zh: 在 TLD 读数仪中加热时释放出这些信息。

segments.text: By measuring the amount of energy released, comparing it to the amount released by the
segments.zh: 通过测量释放的能量，将其与对照剂量计

segments.text: control badge, and running the information through a computer program, the lab can determine
segments.zh: 释放的量进行比较，再将这些信息输入计算机程序，实验室就能确定

segments.text: an individual's exposure.
segments.zh: 个人受到的照射。

segments.text: The results are sent out either monthly or quarterly on these computer-generated reports.
segments.zh: 结果会按月或按季度以这些计算机生成的报告发出，

segments.text: Armstrong listing AL 1499-1 and 1499-2 for each individual.
segments.zh: 即每个人的 Armstrong 清单 AL 1499-1 和 1499-2。

segments.text: The report details the individual's exposure for the last monitoring period and for the
segments.zh: 报告详细列出个人在上一个监测周期内的照射，以及

segments.text: year-to-date exposures.
segments.zh: 本年度迄今为止的照射。

segments.text: The report also breaks out the exposures to the extremities and specific target organs.
segments.zh: 报告还会单独列出四肢和特定靶器官受到的照射。

segments.text: At the end of each year, an AF Form 1527 is sent to document the individual's exposure.
segments.zh: 每年年底，会发出一份 AF Form 1527，记录个人的照射情况。

segments.text: After the form is signed by the RSO, it is sent to the individual to review.
segments.zh: 该表经 RSO 签字后，会发给本人审阅。

segments.text: There are several types of badges used depending on the type of operation being performed.
segments.zh: 根据所进行操作的类型，会使用几种不同类型的剂量计。

segments.text: A whole-body dissimeter badge is the most common and is always required no matter what
segments.zh: 全身剂量计是最常见的，无论佩戴了其他什么类型的剂量计，

segments.text: other type of dissimeter is worn.
segments.zh: 全身剂量计始终都是必须佩戴的。

segments.text: The whole-body dissimeter must be clipped on the front of the body, below the shoulders
segments.zh: 全身剂量计必须夹在身体前面，肩部以下、

segments.text: and above the hips, and is always worn underneath any personal protective equipment in use, especially
segments.zh: 髋部以上，并且始终佩戴在所用的任何个人防护装备的里面，尤其是

segments.text: lead aprons.
segments.zh: 铅围裙。

segments.text: The collar dissimeter is worn on the collar and is required to determine exposures to the
segments.zh: 领部剂量计佩戴在衣领上，当铅围裙盖住全身剂量计时，

segments.text: head and eyes when a lead apron covers the whole-body dissimeter.
segments.zh: 需要用它来确定头部和眼睛受到的照射。

segments.text: A neutron dissimeter is worn flat against the body's midsection, usually with a belt.
segments.zh: 中子剂量计平贴在身体中部佩戴，通常用腰带固定。

segments.text: A ring dissimeter is worn to determine radiation exposures to the hand and forearm, primarily
segments.zh: 指环剂量计用于确定手部和前臂受到的辐射照射，主要

segments.text: in conjunction with fluoroscopy or for personnel who regularly handle radioactive materials.
segments.zh: 用于透视检查，或用于经常接触放射性物质的人员。

segments.text: A dissimeter must never leave the work area and should be stored with the area control
segments.zh: 剂量计绝不能离开工作区域，不用时应与区域对照

segments.text: badge when not in use.
segments.zh: 剂量计存放在一起。

segments.text: Personnel should never allow the TLD to be exposed to heat and sunlight as this may affect
segments.zh: 人员绝不能让 TLD 受热或受到阳光照射，因为这可能影响

segments.text: the readings.
segments.zh: 读数。

segments.text: For personal monitoring, digital alarm dissimeters or DADS are used.
segments.zh: 个人监测会使用数字报警剂量计，即 DAD。

segments.text: These monitors have small ion chambers incorporated into them.
segments.zh: 这些监测仪内部装有小型电离室。

segments.text: They are usually required for personnel who work around high-radiation areas.
segments.zh: 在高辐射区域周围工作的人员通常需要佩戴它们。

segments.text: A digital alarm dissimeter should be used in conjunction with a TLD but never in lieu
segments.zh: 数字报警剂量计应与 TLD 配合使用，但绝不能代替

segments.text: of a TLD.
segments.zh: TLD。

segments.text: It is an important reminder that DADS and TLDs offer no protection for radiation exposures.
segments.zh: 需要提醒的是，DAD 和 TLD 对辐射照射没有任何防护作用。

segments.text: All the required procedures for maximizing the effectiveness of time, distance, shielding
segments.zh: 为最大限度地发挥时间、距离、屏蔽和

segments.text: and contamination control should be spelled out in a unit-specific radiation safety operating
segments.zh: 污染控制的效果，所需的一切程序都应在单位专用的辐射安全操作

segments.text: instruction.
segments.zh: 指令中写明。

segments.text: This OI should be concise but cover shop-specific operations, training requirements, protective
segments.zh: 这份操作指令（OI）应简明扼要，但要涵盖本车间特有的操作、培训要求、所需的防护

segments.text: equipment required, engineering controls and procedures of what to do if you suspect an
segments.zh: 装备、工程控制，以及在你怀疑

segments.text: overexposure.
segments.zh: 过量照射时应采取的程序。

segments.text: If during an operation you identify a potential problem, you must do the minimum, cease operations
segments.zh: 如果在操作过程中发现潜在问题，你至少必须做到：停止操作

segments.text: and secure the area, seek medical assistance if required, contact your supervisor, contact
segments.zh: 并封锁该区域，如有需要寻求医疗救助，联系你的主管，联系

segments.text: the base RSO.
segments.zh: 基地 RSO。

segments.text: For after-duty hour emergencies, the RSO can usually be contacted through the command
segments.zh: 对于下班时间的紧急情况，通常可以通过指挥所

segments.text: post or through the after-hours medical care phone line.
segments.zh: 或下班时间医疗电话热线联系 RSO。

segments.text: Have each individual complete a statement of events including any and all operating parameters,
segments.zh: 让每个人填写一份事件经过陈述，包括所有的操作参数、

segments.text: distances, observations, times and conditions.
segments.zh: 距离、观察情况、时间和条件。

segments.text: Will ionizing radiation hurt my chances for having children?
segments.zh: 电离辐射会影响我生育孩子的机会吗？

segments.text: Ionizing radiation can affect the DNA of a chromosome as previously discussed.
segments.zh: 如前所述，电离辐射会影响染色体的 DNA。

segments.text: Because most mutations are recessive, chance mutation would only present themselves if
segments.zh: 由于大多数突变是隐性的，偶然突变只有在

segments.text: the genes from both parents have the same mutation at the same location on a given pair
segments.zh: 父母双方的基因在某一对染色体的同一位置上

segments.text: of chromosomes.
segments.zh: 发生相同突变时才会表现出来。

segments.text: However unlikely, the effect is cumulative for females as the eggs are developed at
segments.zh: 尽管可能性不大，但对女性来说这种效应是累积的，因为卵子在

segments.text: birth and never replace themselves.
segments.zh: 出生时就已形成，而且永远不会更新。

segments.text: It is another reason to maintain exposures a lara.
segments.zh: 这是保持照射 ALARA 的另一个原因。

segments.text: Will ionizing radiation affect my pregnancy?
segments.zh: 电离辐射会影响我的妊娠吗？

segments.text: A developing fetus is highly susceptible to ionizing radiation, especially in the first
segments.zh: 发育中的胎儿对电离辐射高度敏感，尤其是在怀孕头三个

segments.text: trimester.
segments.zh: 月。

segments.text: It is critical that women who suspect that they may be pregnant get a blood test as soon
segments.zh: 怀疑自己可能怀孕的女性务必尽快验血，

segments.text: as possible in order to be placed in the Air Force Fetal Protection Program.
segments.zh: 以便纳入空军胎儿保护计划。

segments.text: The program requires the workplace to be evaluated for possible factors that may adversely
segments.zh: 该计划要求对工作场所进行评估，找出可能对妊娠产生不利

segments.text: affect pregnancy.
segments.zh: 影响的因素。

segments.text: Based on the workplace factors, work restrictions or modifications may be required.
segments.zh: 根据工作场所的因素，可能需要限制或调整工作。

segments.text: Women who require an x-ray are asked and often tested to ensure they are not pregnant.
segments.zh: 需要做 X 射线检查的女性会被询问，而且常常会接受检测，以确保她们没有怀孕。

segments.text: An overexposure is difficult to detect without instrumentation.
segments.zh: 没有仪器很难发现过量照射。

segments.text: Most people suspect they are exposed only after they realize a mistake may have been
segments.zh: 大多数人只有在意识到可能出了差错之后，

segments.text: made.
segments.zh: 才会怀疑自己受到了照射。

segments.text: A unit left open, a safety device defeated, inadequate area signs and such.
segments.zh: 比如设备没关、安全装置被绕过、区域标志不足等等。

segments.text: All suspected overexposures must be reported and then investigated.
segments.zh: 所有疑似过量照射都必须报告，然后进行调查。

segments.text: Your supervisor, base RSO, or Bioenvironmental Engineering.
segments.zh: 找你的主管、基地 RSO 或生物环境工程部门。

segments.text: They have workplace information and documentation about the radiation exposure potential.
segments.zh: 他们掌握有关辐射照射可能性的工作场所信息和文件。

segments.text: Your base should have a specific instruction about radiation and a lara.
segments.zh: 你们基地应该有关于辐射和 ALARA 的专门指令。

segments.text: For radioactive materials, AFI 40-201, managing radioactive materials in the U.S. Air Force
segments.zh: 对于放射性物质，AFI 40-201《美国空军放射性物质管理》

segments.text: gives excellent guidance on how we manage our radioactive materials.
segments.zh: 为我们如何管理放射性物质提供了出色的指导。

segments.text: Some operations that require radioactive materials have specific technical orders governing proper
segments.zh: 一些需要使用放射性物质的操作有专门的技术规程，规定正确的

segments.text: usage and handling.
segments.zh: 使用和处理方法。

segments.text: Others are restrictive materials and require a radioactive material permit.
segments.zh: 另一些属于受限物质，需要放射性物质许可证。

segments.text: Finally, the governing regulation for all radiation exposures is 10 CFR 20.
segments.zh: 最后，所有辐射照射的管辖法规是 10 CFR 20。

segments.text: In closing, ionizing radiation is a powerful tool but a potential health hazard.
segments.zh: 最后总结一下，电离辐射是一种强大的工具，但也是潜在的健康危害。

segments.text: We need not be fearful of it, but we must respect it.
segments.zh: 我们不必害怕它，但必须尊重它。

segments.text: With informed workers, responsible supervisors and an aggressive safety program, we can keep
segments.zh: 有了知情的工作人员、负责的主管和积极有力的安全计划，我们就能使

segments.text: all exposures to ionizing radiation as low as reasonably achievable.
segments.zh: 所有电离辐射照射保持在合理可行尽量低的水平。
